Kirtipur: Summer Institute of Linguistics and Institute of Nepal Studies, Tribhuvan University. 40 pp. [SIL Language & Culture Archives scan, 43 PDF pp., CC BY-NC-SA; downloaded via the Internet Archive copy of the sil.org reapdata URL; scanned at 300 dpi]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: HathiTrust digitized, search-only (in copyright); interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: No section on stress/accent and no statement of where stress falls (contents: I Introduction, II Consonants, III Vowels, IV Syllables). Stress is mentioned only as a conditioning factor: p.30 'the following three vowels [/i e u/] have the illustrated free variants in unstressed syllables only'; p.32 'Lengthened vowels in Tharu are conditioned by stress and syllable shape. Vowels in open stressed syllables will receive the maximum length, while vowels in closed unstressed syllables will receive the minimum length.. <In the above cases, the underlined syllable is the stressed syllable>'. sources.citation: Trail, Ronald L. (ed.). 1973. Patterns in clause, sentence, and discourse in selected languages of India and Nepal, Part IV: Word lists. Norman: SIL, University of Oklahoma. sources.note: Introduction gives only location (Devauli village), speaker numbers, a phoneme chart and notes on aspiration and nasalization; nothing on stress.
